prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: polished, shippable desktop website first-viewport decision comp, exact 16:10 landscape aspect ratio
Primary request: Design a visually distinctive homepage first viewport for DIREPAIR, an Indonesian specialist repair service for non-mainstream electronics, using Jakarta transit wayfinding and route-diagram logic as the visual language, while making it unmistakably an electronics repair service and never a transport app.
Scene/backdrop: warm paper #F7F4EA full-bleed webpage canvas with subtle analog ticket-paper grain, otherwise flat clean color fields.
Subject and information architecture: One large, dominant service-route atlas must cross the entire viewport edge to edge and occupy the whole composition—not a standard split hero and not a card grid. A strong deep route-blue repair line visibly starts at device intake, branches through diagnosis and quotation, converges through repair, and reaches finish. Integrate simplified specialist-electronics pictograms and small tool/connector symbols into stations: retro camera, handheld game console, turntable, projector, audio unit, and circuit board, clearly signaling repair. Use solid colored route lines, station dots, transfer rings, elbows, compact route codes, diagnostic symbols, screws, cable traces, and small technical annotations. The route map itself is the page architecture.
Headline and CTA integration: Make a large elegant Indonesian headline part of the map, as though it is a wayfinding destination label: "Elektronik unik, kembali berfungsi." Integrate the exact CTA "Mulai diagnosis" into a ticket-yellow station/wayfinding button connected directly to the intake route. Render brand word "DIREPAIR" exactly once as a compact masthead at top left, never repeated.
Required labels and copy: use these exact, legible labels only: "DIREPAIR"; "Elektronik unik, kembali berfungsi."; "Mulai diagnosis"; station labels "Terima perangkat", "Diagnosis", "Penawaran", "Perbaikan", "Selesai"; station codes "IN-01", "DG-02", "QT-03", "RP-04", "OK-05"; a compact paper repair ticket with "TIKET SERVIS", "Perangkat", "Keluhan", "Status: pemeriksaan awal". Keep ticket details sparse and legible. Do not invent prices, statistics, testimonials, ratings, guarantees, phone numbers, addresses, menu items, or extra marketing claims.
Style/medium: realistic high-fidelity product UI mockup, editorial Swiss-modern wayfinding meets Jakarta commuter-route signage and Indonesian workshop intake ticket. Flat vector-like geometry, precise alignment, sophisticated typography, tactile paper note, restrained technical micro-details. Modern, elegant, locally resonant, crafted by a human design team, production-feasible HTML/CSS, not concept art.
Composition/framing: exact 16:10 landscape desktop viewport, full browser-content crop without device frame. Service-route atlas flows diagonally and horizontally across the entire canvas, with purposeful asymmetry, branching and reconnection. Headline, CTA, service ticket, and small navigation cues are embedded at route junctions rather than placed in conventional hero columns. Spacious but information-rich, strong visual hierarchy, responsive-feeling edge behavior, balanced crop at viewport edges.
Color palette: only deep route blue #102A43, warm paper #F7F4EA, red #D8432F, ticket yellow #F0C44D, green #3B7C72, plus white only where needed for accessible contrast. Flat colors only, absolutely no gradients.
Typography: crisp modern grotesk sans serif paired with compact monospaced station codes; large headline highly legible; accessible contrast; exact text spelling.
Constraints: exactly one webpage first viewport; CTA text must be exactly "Mulai diagnosis"; "DIREPAIR" appears exactly once; map is the dominant composition; unmistakably electronics repair; polished enough to ship; no photographs or faces; no fake claims; no ratings; no testimonials; no unrelated logos; no watermark; no browser/device mockup frame.
Avoid: standard left-copy/right-image split hero; card grid; dashboard; transit app UI; train illustrations; metro vehicles; maps of real geography; excessive rounded cards; glassmorphism; gradients; 3D; glossy effects; fake body text; lorem ipsum; tiny unreadable copy; random glyphs; duplicate words; AI-looking ornamental clutter.
